title: vehicle-sil request file (vehicle_sil_launch run --request, check --request), format 1
description: What to run, written down: the variant, the scenario and its parameters, the participants left out or started by hand, where the networks are connected outside the simulation, and the speed. One file serves a test bench or a kind of run, for every configuration used there. `vehicle_sil_launch run --request <this file> <configuration>` reads it; an argument of the command line wins over the file, field by field. This schema finds unknown keys and values of the wrong form while you write. Write JSON: vehicle_sil_launch may read a looser form, but that is no promise, and other tools read JSON only. A key that is not meant is left out (null is no value). It cannot see the configuration: whether the variant, the participants and the networks exist is what `vehicle_sil_launch check --request <this file> <configuration>` says. The configuration file, the log directory, the timeline, the wall-clock time limit and the control server are not in this file: they are arguments. The manual is docs/simulation-run.md of vehicle-sil.

$schema.description: The path or URL of this schema, for an editor. vehicle_sil_launch does not read it.

variant.description: The variant of the configuration to check or run (--variant).

propertyNames.description: A parameter's name: letters, digits and _ (not a digit first).

additionalProperties.description: One value: a number, true or false, or a text. It cannot use another parameter (${...}).

params.description: Values of the scenario's parameters ${name}, over the scenario's, the configuration's and the variant's params. --param <name>=<value> replaces one by name. Used only when a scenario runs: without a scenario they are ignored with the note request-params-unused. If the file names the scenario itself, a name that scenario does not have is a usage error; if the scenario comes from --scenario, it is ignored with the same note (one file serves several scenarios).

scenario.description: The scenario file to check and run (--scenario). A relative path is from the directory of the configuration file (unlike --scenario, which is from the working directory).

disable.description: Participants to leave out (--disable). Added to those of the command line; --enable <name> or --manual <name> there wins for that name. A name that the configuration does not have is an error, and so is a name that is also in enable or manual.

enable.description: Participants to take in (--enable). Added to those of the command line; --disable <name> there wins for that name. A name that the configuration does not have is an error.

manual.description: Participants that you start yourself (--manual). Added to those of the command line; --disable <name> there wins for that name. A name that the configuration does not have is an error.

additionalProperties.description: The target, as --connect <network>=<target> takes it (`vehicle_sil_launch connections <configuration>` lists those of this computer). "none": SIL Kit only, as if the network was not written.

connect.description: Where each network is connected outside the simulation, by the network's name (--connect). --connect <network>=<target> replaces the target of that network, and --connect <network>=none takes it away for one run. A network that the configuration does not have is left out with the note connect-network-unused (one file serves several configurations).

time_policy.description: The time of a run that is connected outside the simulation (--time-policy). realtime (the default): it goes at speed 1. free: the speed and the time can be changed; everyone who uses this file then runs without that guard, and the notes of such a run name this file.

speed.description: Simulation seconds per wall-clock second (1: real time, 2: twice as fast), or "max": as fast as possible (--speed). Replaces speed in the configuration.

start_paused.description: true: stand still at 0 until a resume or step command (--start-paused; a run then needs --stdin-commands or --control). false is as if the key was not written: --start-paused still counts.

stop_at_ms.description: Exact automatic stop time in virtual milliseconds since the start. Omit to run without an automatic stop.

late_tolerance_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds of lateness before a paced step counts as late.

strict.description: true: fail on warnings too (--strict). false is as if the key was not written: --strict still counts.
